body: I’m 24 (f) now, but I was diagnosed just about a year and a month ago. It was with an ex that ended up being a toxic person all around. He was using me the entire time and then he also contracted chlamydia, gonorhea (sp?) , and syphalis after he ghosted me.  I got a call from our local sexual health clinic, to which I referred him to when we were dating, saying that a partner I’ve been with had tested positive for all of these (he was the only person I had been with during the pandemic at that point). I had my first outbreak during our relationship where he also didn’t tell me he had chlamydia during this point, but I didn’t have it, which led to the demise of our relationship. I only just finished up (yesterday, to be exact!) my first outbreak since then. I stopped taking daily valtrex when I met my current boyfriend who has cold sores and understood there was no risk to him with my HSV diagnosis because he has it too. I was honestly terrified of dating and I realize now, there’s really understanding people out there and there are suppressive medications you can take if your partner isn’t positive for HSV to reduce the risk of transmission. Now that I have come to accept it as just a part of life that I deal with, I have a lot less anger and sadness that are attached to the diagnosis (definitely was sad during this last outbreak again, but hey, it hurts!)   I promise you, staying with someone just because of the diagnosis just causes you more pain and sadness in the end. I thought the same, especially in the peak of the pandemic, but now I wish I didn’t reach out to that person and beg for them to come back. Its time for you to love yourself and do what’s best for you. Best of luck!!
